rounds.text: Johnsoncab Electricals Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental performance, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 44% and a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 145% [E13, E16]. The company generates world-class returns, boasting an ROE of 58.6% and a ROCE of 27.6%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks where sector median ROCE sits at just 13.4% [E8, E9, E12, E43]. This momentum is underpinned by operational expansion, with operating margins expanding by 5 percentage points over three years to reach 12% in March 2026 [E19]. Furthermore, the broader macro environment provides strong backing, as the Capital Goods sector operates in a clear tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.57 and sector median profit growth of 23.0% [E39, E40, E41]. Valuation metrics indicate significant mispricing, as a reverse DCF shows the current market price only implies 7.7% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0%, alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value pointing to a substantial margin of safety of 52.6% [E28, E29, E30]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -20 Cr in March 2026 and debt to equity stands at an elevated 2.50x [E22, E24].

Johnsoncab Electricals Ltd carries severe financial and operational risks that undermine its reported profitability. Most notably, cash conversion stands at a deeply negative -1.54x for March 2026, driven by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -20 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -37 Cr [E21, E22, E23]. This stark divergence between accounting profits and actual cash generation raises serious questions about earnings quality. Furthermore, the company's leverage has escalated dangerously, with debt to equity reaching 2.50x as borrowings nearly doubled to Rs 80 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 42 Cr a year prior [E24, E25]. This high debt load, where liabilities exceed net worth, exposes the business to acute solvency and liquidity pressures [E24]. Operational stability is also compromised by an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend over the last three years [E20], alongside a total absence of shareholder cash returns, reflected in a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: the company demonstrates impressive multi-year sales and profit growth, high historical return on equity metrics, and trades at an 18.8x P/E with a reverse DCF implying modest required growth [E1, E13, E15, E18, E30].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -20 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -37 Cr in March 2026, leading to a negative cash conversion of -1.54x [E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: debt to equity is 2.50x with borrowings at Rs 80 Cr, and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3, E24, E25]. However, these short-term cash pressures and high leverage are more than offset by blistering top and bottom-line expansion, with 3-year compounded sales growth at 44% and profit growth at 81%, accelerating to 51% and 145% respectively over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16]. Conceded: the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent [E20], yet operating margin has climbed to 12% in March 2026 from 7% three years earlier [E19]. Furthermore, the market price of Rs 238 sits well below the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 503, offering a substantial 52.6% margin of safety [E28, E29]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that the current price only requires a modest 7.7% earnings growth against the 18.0% base case, proving the valuation heavily under-appreciates the company's structural momentum [E30].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales and profit growth stand at 44% and 81% respectively, accelerating to 51% and 145% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16], and operating margin has climbed to 12% in March 2026 from 7% three years earlier [E19]. However, this rapid top-line expansion has coincided with alarming cash destruction, evidenced by a negative cash conversion of -1.54x, negative operating cash flow of Rs -20 Cr, and negative free cash flow of Rs -37 Cr in March 2026 [E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value is Rs 503 and the reverse DCF implies a modest 7.7% earnings growth [E28, E30]. Yet this valuation ignores severe balance sheet stress, as borrowings nearly doubled from Rs 42 Cr to Rs 80 Cr in a single year, pushing debt-to-equity to 2.50x where debt actively exceeds net worth [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the yearly operating-margin trend is explicitly inconsistent over the last three years [E20], and the stock pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E3], leaving shareholders exposed to high financial leverage without immediate cash returns.
